subject: Chemistry
unit: Unit XVI — Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
title: Phenol Acidity: Resonance Stabilization & Substituent Effects
topics: Acidity Comparison (pK_a): Picric Acid (0.38) > Phenol (9.98) > Water (15.7) > Ethanol (16.0)
5.1 Resonance Stabilization of the Phenoxide Anion (Ph-O⁻) vs Localized Alkoxide (R-O⁻)
5.2 Substituent Effects: Electron-Withdrawing (-M/-I) Increase Acidity; Electron-Donating (+M/+I) Decrease Acidity
Nitrophenol Acidity Spectrum (pK_a): Picric Acid (0.38) > 2,4-Dinitro (4.0) > p-Nitro (7.15) > o-Nitro (7.23) > m-Nitro (8.35) > Phenol (9.98)
The Ortho- vs Para-Nitrophenol Paradox (Intramolecular H-Bonding in o-Nitrophenol hinders deprotonation & confers steam volatility)
quickSummary: Phenol (pK_a ~10) is 10⁶ times more acidic than ethanol (pK_a ~16) because the phenoxide anion is resonance-stabilized. -M/-I groups (-NO₂) increase acidity (Picric acid pK_a = 0.38). p-Nitrophenol is more acidic than o-nitrophenol because o-nitrophenol forms intramolecular H-bonds (also making it steam-volatile).
summary: Master phenoxide resonance stabilization, substituent electronic effects, and nitrophenol acidity rankings.

conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 Substituent Effects & The Nitrophenol Spectrum
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
NITROPHENOL ACIDITY SPECTRUM ($\text{p}K_a$)
                   
   2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (Picric Acid, 0.38) > 2,4-Dinitrophenol (4.0) > *p*-Nitrophenol (7.15) > *o*-Nitrophenol (7.23) > *m*-Nitrophenol (8.35) > Phenol (9.98)

• o- vs p-Nitrophenol Paradox: p-Nitrophenol is slightly MORE acidic than o-nitrophenol because o-nitrophenol forms Intramolecular H-bonds hindering proton loss.
• Steam Volatility: o-Nitrophenol has intramolecular H-bonds (steam volatile); p-nitrophenol has intermolecular H-bonds (higher BP, non-volatile).

quickRevision: Phenol is 10⁶x more acidic than ethanol due to phenoxide resonance.
-NO₂ at o/p positions increases acidity via -M and -I effects.
p-Nitrophenol is slightly more acidic than o-nitrophenol.
